questions.enonce_markdown:
The functions $f$ and $g$ are defined as $f: x \mapsto 3x + 1$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and $g: x \mapsto \dfrac{1}{f(x)}$.

(a) Find $f(2)$.

(b) State the domain of $f(x)$.

(c) Evaluate $g(1)$.

(d) Find $f^{-1}(x)$.

(e) Find $gf(x)$ and state its domain.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a)** $f(2) = 3(2) + 1 = 7$.

**(b)** $f(x) = 3x + 1$ is defined for every real number, so the domain of $f$ is $\mathbb{R}$ (all real values of $x$).

**(c)** $g(1) = \dfrac{1}{f(1)} = \dfrac{1}{3(1) + 1} = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

**(d)** Let $y = 3x + 1$. Make $x$ the subject: $x = \dfrac{y - 1}{3}$. So $f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{x - 1}{3}$.

**(e)** $g(x) = \dfrac{1}{3x + 1}$, so $gf(x) = g(f(x)) = g(3x + 1) = \dfrac{1}{3(3x + 1) + 1} = \dfrac{1}{9x + 4}$.

The expression is not defined when the denominator is zero: $9x + 4 = 0$, that is $x = -\dfrac{4}{9}$.

**Answer:** $gf(x) = \dfrac{1}{9x + 4}$, with domain $x \in \mathbb{R}$, $x \neq -\dfrac{4}{9}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Using a ruler and a pair of compasses only:

(a) Construct triangle $PQR$ in which $PQ = 5\,\mathrm{cm}$, $QR = 4\,\mathrm{cm}$ and angle $PQR = 60^\circ$.

(b) Bisect any two sides of triangle $PQR$.

(c) Construct a circle with centre $O$, such that the circle passes through the vertices $P$, $Q$ and $R$. *[15 marks for the whole question B2]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Construction of the triangle.**

1. Draw a line and mark $Q$. With the compasses set to $5\,\mathrm{cm}$, mark $P$ on the line, so $PQ = 5\,\mathrm{cm}$.
2. With the compass point at $Q$ and any radius, draw an arc cutting $QP$ at $X$. With the same radius and the point at $X$, cut that arc at $Y$. Then $\angle XQY = 60^\circ$.
3. Draw the ray $QY$. With the compass point at $Q$ and radius $4\,\mathrm{cm}$, mark $R$ on the ray, so $QR = 4\,\mathrm{cm}$.
4. Join $P$ to $R$.

**(b) Bisecting two sides.** For the side $PQ$: with the compass point at $P$ then at $Q$, using the same radius (more than half of $PQ$), draw arcs above and below $PQ$; they cross at two points. Join these two points: this is the perpendicular bisector of $PQ$. Repeat for the side $QR$ (or $PR$). Keep all construction arcs visible.

**(c) The circumcircle.** The two perpendicular bisectors meet at the point $O$, which is equidistant from $P$, $Q$ and $R$. Place the compass point at $O$, open it to $OP$ (or $OQ$, or $OR$) and draw the circle: it passes through $P$, $Q$ and $R$.

**Check of the result.** By the cosine rule $PR^2 = 5^2 + 4^2 - 2(5)(4)\cos 60^\circ = 21$, so $PR \approx 4.58\,\mathrm{cm}$. The radius of the circle is $\dfrac{PR}{2\sin 60^\circ} = \sqrt{7} \approx 2.65\,\mathrm{cm}$, so the circle you draw should have a radius of about $2.6\,\mathrm{cm}$. *(Construction to be drawn by the candidate.)*
